commitResults.messageBody:

3. Added print statements to greet user and exit
4. Updated README.md to reflect changes above

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-1: Add Echo functionality
commitResults.messageBody:
HappyBot now echo commands entered by the user.
Program exits when user types "bye"

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-2: Implement Add and List Task
commitResults.messageBody:
1. New Class Task is created that has a description field
2. User input serve as description for new task added
3. If user types "list", program will list all tasks added
4. All tasks stored in a fixed size array of size 100
	* Assumption is that number of task will not exceed 100
5. "bye" to terminate program

3. Abstracted logic from main into modular functions

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement ToDos, Events and Deadlines
Add HappyBot Exception to handle user input error
Add Support for deleting tasks from list
commitResults.messageBody: Now an ArrayList is used to store tasks instead of a fixed size array

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix coding standard violations
Add saving and loading of tasks to a data file
commitResults.messageBody:
HappyBot holds the task list only in memory, so every task is lost on
exit and the user must retype the whole list on each run.

Add a Storage class that writes the list to data/HappyBot.txt
whenever it changes and reads it back on startup, saving through a
temporary file that is renamed over the data file so an interrupted
save cannot truncate saved tasks.

Create the data folder on first save, skip unreadable lines,
and ignore /data/ since it is generated at runtime.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-7'
Add Date and Time for tasks
Merge branch 'branch-Level-8'
Make HappyBot an object that owns its task list
commitResults.messageBody:
HappyBot is a bag of static methods that pass the task list and the
Storage to each other as parameters. The A-MoreOOP task splits its
responsibilities into Ui, Storage, Parser and TaskList classes, and each
of those extractions would have to add one more parameter to every such
method, only to take it away again once an object can hold it in a
field.

Reshape the main class first, before extracting anything, so that every
later extraction replaces a field instead of threading a parameter
through the whole class. HappyBot now creates its Storage and its task
list in a constructor, runs the command loop in an instance method, and
leaves main() with a single statement.

Load the saved tasks in run() rather than in the constructor, because
the notice about unreadable saved data has to appear after the welcome
message.

Compile src/main/java/*.java in the UI test plan's build command, so the
classes added by later steps need no further edit to that command.
Console output is unchanged and all 19 UI test cases still pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Ui class from HappyBot
commitResults.messageBody:
HappyBot decides what a command means and, in the same methods, spells
out how the answer looks on screen. The divider line and the reply
wording are therefore spread over a dozen methods, and a change to the
look of one reply means hunting through logic to find it.

Move every console interaction into a new Ui class: reading a command,
the welcome and farewell messages, the task listing, the confirmation
after each change, and the error and notice messages. Give it one
method per reply, so a caller asks for a reply by name and never sees a
divider or a leading space. The Scanner moves there too, because
reading from the user is an interaction with the user.

Hand Ui the deadlines of a due command in a LinkedHashMap keyed by task
number. A deadline is marked or deleted by its number in the full list,
so the number cannot be recovered from the position in the filtered
listing and has to travel with the task.

Leave the wording of rejected commands in HappyBot, where the rule that
rejects the command lives; Ui only adds the "Oops!" prefix and the
dividers around it. This keeps a message next to the check that
produces it, ready to move to Parser with that check later.

HappyBot is now free of System.out and 70 lines shorter. Console output
is unchanged and all 19 UI test cases still pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: route every reply through one exit point
commitResults.messageBody:
Three loose ends were left by the extraction of Ui.

The two listing methods printed `builder + DIVIDER`. That reads as if a
StringBuilder is being handed to println, which it is not: a `+` with a
String operand converts the builder to a String first, and println is
then given that String. Call toString() so the conversion is written
down rather than implied.

Those two methods were also the only ones closing their own block, which
is why the conversion was there at all. Drop the line break that
formatEntry added to every task line, join the lines in the caller, and
end both listings with showReply() like every other reply. showReply is
now the single place that writes a closing divider, for all nine
replies.

Inline showNotice() into the two methods that called it. A private
one-liner with two callers hides more than it saves, unlike showReply,
which states a rule once instead of nine times.

Record in the test plan that the two startup notices are checked by
hand. They predate this work, but no automated case can reach them: the
run command deletes the data file before every case, while both notices
need saved data that is already present and already broken. Both were
run by hand against a scratch data file and print as before.

Console output is unchanged and all 19 UI test cases still pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser class from HappyBot
commitResults.messageBody:
The command loop held about seventy lines of string handling: it hunted
for " /by ", " /from " and " /to ", cut descriptions out of the text,
checked each piece for blanks, and read dates, all inside the switch
that also decided what each command does. Adding a command meant adding
another block of text handling to a method already too long to read.

Move all of it into a new Parser class. Each method takes command text
and returns what the command names: a command word, a task number, a
date, or a ready-made task. The switch is now one line per command, so
what a command does is visible without reading how its text is picked
apart.

Report an unreadable date as a HappyBotException carrying the date
hint, rather than letting DateTimeParseException reach the loop. A
command that cannot be understood is one kind of failure whatever the
cause, so the loop no longer needs a second catch block and no other
class needs to know that dates are parsed with java.time.

Take the task number from the command body rather than by cutting the
command word off the input again, and reject an out-of-range number in
one new getTask() method instead of in three copies. Delete by
position, not by value, because List.remove(Object) would search for an
equal task instead of removing the one that was chosen.

HappyBot is down to 239 lines from 367. Console output is unchanged:
all 19 UI test cases pass and the manual notice check still prints as
before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList class from HappyBot
commitResults.messageBody:
HappyBot held a raw List<Task> and worked on it directly. Every place
that took a task number subtracted one from it, the check for a number
that belongs to no task sat in HappyBot, and the search behind the due
command walked the list with an index so it could remember which number
each deadline had. The rule that a task is named from the outside by its
position, counted from one, was therefore spread across the class that
should only be deciding what a command does.

Move the tasks and that rule into a new TaskList class, which offers
add(), get(), delete(), size(), isEmpty() and findDeadlinesDueOn().
Only TaskList converts a task number into a position, and it refuses a
number no task holds, so the check that was repeated three times is
written once.

Hand out the tasks as an unmodifiable view for displaying and saving,
and copy the tasks given to the constructor. The list then cannot be
changed behind TaskList's back, and Ui and Storage keep working with a
plain List instead of depending on a class they have no use for.

HappyBot is now 209 lines and imports nothing but IOException, Path and
LocalDate: it creates the four objects, asks Parser what a command
means, asks TaskList to carry it out, and asks Ui to report it.

Console output is unchanged. All 19 UI test cases pass, both startup
notices still print, and a save followed by a restart reloads the tasks
as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
